abort.cannot_connect_reason: Could not set up the device at {host}: {reason}. The Home Assistant log has the details.
abort.no_devices_found: No WiZ devices answered, neither to a broadcast nor to a direct query of every address on your network. Make sure the devices are powered and on the same network as Home Assistant, or enter the IP address yourself.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: That IP address belongs to a different WiZ device. Please reconfigure against the same device.

error.bulb_time_out: The device did not answer on UDP port 38899. Check the IP address, that the device is powered, and that nothing blocks UDP between Home Assistant and the device.
error.cannot_connect: Something at that address refused UDP port 38899. It is probably not a WiZ device, or the IP address is wrong.
error.invalid_key_format: The signing key should be the hex string from the WiZ app export (32 hex characters, no prefix).
error.invalid_signing_key: The device rejected the signing key. Either the key is wrong (it is one key per WiZ home) or the Home Assistant clock is more than about a minute off.
error.no_wiz_light: The device answered, but not like a WiZ device. The Home Assistant log has the raw answer.
error.signing_required: This device only answers signed requests. Enter the signing key.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log

discovery_confirm.description: Do you want to set up {name} ({host})?

data_description.signing_key: The udp_signing_key value from the WiZ app's local integration export. It is the same for every device in a WiZ home.

reauth_confirm.description: {name} ({host}) runs firmware that only accepts signed commands, and it needs a valid signing key. If you already entered the right key, check that the Home Assistant clock is correct: the device rejects requests that are more than about a minute old.
reauth_confirm.title: WiZ signing key

data_description.signing_key: Only needed for firmware that requires signed commands. Leave empty to remove it.
The udp_signing_key value from the WiZ app's local integration export. It is the same for every device in a WiZ home.

signing_key.description: {name} ({host}) runs firmware that only accepts signed commands. Without the key Home Assistant can read its state but cannot control it. Leave the field empty to add it anyway.
signing_key.title: Signing key required

data_description.host: Leave empty to search the network.
data_description.signing_key: Only needed for newer firmware that requires signed commands: the udp_signing_key from the WiZ app's local integration export.

user.description: If you leave the IP address empty, Home Assistant searches the network, using both a broadcast and a direct query of every address on your subnet.

cannot_connect.message: Failed to connect to the WiZ device at {ip_address}: {error}

not_supported.message: The WiZ device does not support this command

signature_rejected.message: {name} ({ip_address}) rejected the signing key. Either the key is wrong or the Home Assistant clock is off. Re-enter the key when Home Assistant asks for it.

signing_key_required.message: {name} ({ip_address}) only accepts signed commands. Enter the signing key from the WiZ app when Home Assistant asks for it.

timeout.message: Timed out waiting for {name} ({ip_address}) to respond

update_failed.message: Failed to update the WiZ device at {ip_address}: {error}
